explanation: Gift-giving is a welcomed, relationship-building gesture in Indonesia, and gifts should be given and received with the right hand or both hands, since the left hand is considered unclean for offering items. Given Indonesia's large Muslim-majority population, it's also safest to avoid alcohol and pork products as gifts and to keep gifts modest rather than lavish. The halal-gift guidance is a reasonable extension of well-documented Islamic-influenced norms, though a source addressing gift-giving in Indonesia specifically wasn't found this session.
local_tip: Offer and receive gifts with your right hand or both hands, keep them modest, and avoid alcohol or pork products for Muslim recipients.

also_check.note: Gift-giving is highly ritualized; use both hands and avoid sets of four items (an unlucky number).
Gifts in formal business settings can seem inappropriate unless a relationship is already established.
Gifts are appreciated but should be halal, avoiding alcohol or pork, and given with the right hand.

sources.title: Why visitors to Indonesia should avoid using their left hand
